text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An editorial urged the new government to restore public order and implement sound economic policies.

- Parliament decided to increase the number of members on the board of state television to 21 from 11 in a bid to get rid of the general director, widely seen as supporting former president Sali Berisha and his Democratic Party.
- Albanian President Rexhep Mejdani in an interview announced the election of a new supreme council of justice in order to open the way to real democratic reform in the legal system.
- If the Socialists modify constitutional laws the Democratic Party will refuse to take their seats in parliament, the party's secretary for public relations Vili Minarolli said.
- Interior deputy minister Sokol Bare said police would start to collect arms as soon as parliament passed the law on disarming the population.
- Prime Minister Fatos Nano said he was happy that the international community was determined to help Albania to rebuild its economy and democratic institutions.

- The central bank governor Qamil Tusha told a news conference that the stronger lek was due to psychological factors. The Lek firmed to 139 to the dollar in Tirana's informal street market on Thursday from 170 last week.
- Qazim Gjonaj, head of the Tirana court, slammed the Justice Minister's order to suspend all judicial processes for an unspecified period of time as illegal.
- Since July more than 6,000 Albanian immigrants have been expelled from Greece.
- The disarmament of the population has to start in the southern part of Albania with its many criminal gangs, the chief of Tirana police Pashk Tusha says in an interview.

- The commitment and the tenacity of former president Sali Berisha were vital to Albania's position in the Council of Europe, the president of the Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly Leni Fisher said in a letter sent to Berisha.
